subject: Failover handoff latency - request to exclude 2026-02-02 partial window from uptime calculation
messages:
From: Sara Norrell <sara.n@acmecloud.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-02T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Intermittent latency spike during provider failover (RF-8421)

Hi Vivek,

We observed an ~8-minute latency spike (09:07–09:15 EST) impacting 30% of requests to our /api/generate endpoint. Our edge logs and traceroutes show a multi-hop handoff that looks like EdgeStream's CDN initiated failover to a backup POP. The spike aligns with a cache re-population (lots of 503/504s followed by 200s).

Can you confirm how Redwood attributes this to our SLO? Specifically:
- Does a third-party CDN failover count as a third-party outage that can be excluded from uptime calculations?
- If it's a partial degradation (30% of traffic), how will the credit be apportioned?

I've attached the trimmed edge logs and our traceroute (acme-incident-log-20260202.csv).

We'd like to request exclusion of the 09:07–09:15 window from the uptime tally if EdgeStream confirms a failover maintenance or automated failover.

Thanks,

Sara Norrell
Infra Ops, Acme Cloud
sara.n@acmecloud.com
Attachments: acme-incident-log-20260202.csv (text/csv, 124KB)

Subject: Re: Intermittent latency spike during provider failover (RF-8421)

Sara —

Thanks for the details and the logs. We'll take a look; copied Marissa (SRE lead, uptime accounting) and Ben (sales/contract) so we can coordinate any SLA follow-up.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Marissa will run an SLO apportionment over the 09:00–09:30 window and cross-check our ingested request sampling with your edge logs.
- If EdgeStream confirms scheduled maintenance or an automated failover that sits outside our control plane, we'll evaluate exclusion per section 4.3 of the SLA.

Could you also share the EdgeStream incident id if you have it, and permission for us to contact their ops team directly? That will speed confirmation.

I'll follow up once we have a preliminary apportionment.

— Vivek

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-02-03T11:22:00-05:00
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent latency spike during provider failover (RF-8421) — preliminary apportionment

Vivek / Sara —

Forwarding our preliminary apportionment. Summary below; full math and chart are attached (redwood-slo-calculation-fig1.png).

Summary:
- Window analyzed: 09:00–09:30 EST (2026-02-02)
- Observed impact: 09:07–09:15 EST with elevated p50/p95 and increased 5xxs. Traffic sampling indicates ~28–33% of overall requests experienced degraded latency.
- Root cause signals: simultaneous route withdrawals to a subset of EdgeStream POPs and cache-miss surge consistent with a failover handoff.

Interpretation against our SLA (section 4.3 "Third-party provider events"):
- If EdgeStream's action was a scheduled maintenance announced to customers, we treat it as a third-party maintenance and may exclude the window from the uptime tally.
- If it was an automated failover triggered by an EdgeStream internal condition (unannounced), it remains a third-party outage but not a scheduled maintenance; per SLA we still consider third-party outages for apportionment but not automatically excluded.

Proposal (to be agreed with Acme):
- Pending EdgeStream confirmation of a scheduled maintenance, exclude the full 09:07–09:15 window.
- If EdgeStream confirms an automated failover (no scheduled maintenance), classify as partial degradation and apportion credit prorated by impacted traffic: we propose apportionment factor = 0.32 (32%) resulting in a credit equivalent to 32% of the downtime contribution for that window.

Notes on calculation: we used request-weighted p95 deltas and matched timestamps to your traceroutes; see attached figure.

Action items:
- Sara: please share EdgeStream incident id or permission for Redwood to open a liaison ticket with them.
- Ben/Vivek: if Acme accepts the proposed apportionment approach, we'll draft the formal credit calculation and an SLA amendment statement for record.

Attachments: redwood-slo-calculation-fig1.png (image/png, 86KB)
